sentences.en: Hear me, O spirits of water, earth, fire, and air, angels of the heavens and demons of the underworld.
sentences.zh: 听好了，水、土、火、气的精灵，天堂的天使和地狱的恶魔。

sentences.en: I call upon you to bring ruin and destruction onto Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin,
sentences.zh: 我召唤你们给弗拉基米尔·弗拉基米罗维奇·普京带来毁灭和灾难，

sentences.en: war maker, murderer, and despot, so that the wickedness, pain, and death he unleashes shall return to him tenfold.
sentences.zh: 这个战争贩子、杀人犯和暴君，让他所释放的邪恶、痛苦和死亡十倍地回到他自己身上。

sentences.en: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin, you are cursed.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·弗拉基米罗维奇·普京，你被诅咒了。

sentences.en: You are bound.
sentences.zh: 你被束缚了。

sentences.en: May you choke on the seeds of sunflowers.
sentences.zh: 愿你被向日葵的种子噎死。

sentences.en: May your soldiers refuse to fight.
sentences.zh: 愿你的士兵拒绝战斗。

sentences.en: May your people rise up against you, break your bones, and cast you down into dust and ashes.
sentences.zh: 愿你的人民起来反抗你，打断你的骨头，将你抛入尘土和灰烬之中。

sentences.en: Gurry, gurry, gurry.
sentences.zh: 咕噜，咕噜，咕噜。

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That was a spell.
sentences.zh: 那是一个咒语。

sentences.en: So that was our first ever spell, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，那是我们有史以来的第一个咒语。

sentences.en: That was a hex that is being placed every Saturday night at 7.33 p.m.
sentences.zh: 那是一个每周六晚上7点33分施下的诅咒，

sentences.en: Eastern Daylight Time in the United States on Vladimir Putin by the witches of the world.
sentences.zh: 美国东部夏令时间，由世界各地的女巫对弗拉基米尔·普京施下。

sentences.en: So if you want to join in, Tom, just follow the hashtag.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想加入，汤姆，只要关注这个标签就行了。

sentences.en: Or maybe the listeners could join in.
sentences.zh: 或者也许听众们也可以加入。

sentences.en: Just follow the hashtag, hexputin.
sentences.zh: 只要关注标签：诅咒普京（hexputin）。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And you can hex him too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以诅咒他。

sentences.en: What is it with the getting him to choke on sunflower seeds?
sentences.zh: 让他被向日葵种子噎住是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So sunflower seeds is a big thing.
sentences.zh: 向日葵种子是一件大事。

sentences.en: So if you may have seen a clip in one of those sort of clips that was doing the rounds on social media of an elderly woman offering sunflower seeds to Russian soldiers,
sentences.zh: 如果你在社交媒体上流传的那些片段中看到过一位老妇人给俄罗斯士兵提供向日葵种子的视频，

sentences.en: and she says to them, put them in your pockets, because then when you're dead, something will grow in the land where your blood waters the soil or something like that.
sentences.zh: 她对他们说，把它们装进口袋，因为当你死后，你的鲜血浇灌的土地上就会长出东西，或者类似的话。

sentences.en: So sunflower seeds are quite a big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以向日葵种子意义重大。

sentences.en: And maybe if we had a decent guest, he would be able to tell us whether sunflower seeds carried great occult meaning.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要是有个像样的嘉宾，他或许能告诉我们向日葵种子是否具有重大的神秘学意义。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, as it happens, we do have a great gueSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，巧的是，我们确实有一位伟大的嘉宾。

sentences.en: We have the great Dr. Francis Young, who I would say, of all the people I follow on Twitter, is the most Magus-like.
sentences.zh: 我们有伟大的弗朗西斯·杨博士，我会说，在我关注的所有推特用户中，他是最像法师的一位。

sentences.en: Magus-like, wow.
sentences.zh: 像法师，哇。

sentences.en: His Twitter feed is like – well, I think Merlin would really enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 他的推特动态就像——嗯，我想梅林一定会很喜欢。

sentences.en: He's necromantic.
sentences.zh: 他精通死灵术。

sentences.en: Well, he talks about medieval saints, so you'd like that, Lithuanian grammar, Roman mosaics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他谈论中世纪圣徒，所以你会喜欢的，还有立陶宛语语法、罗马马赛克。

sentences.en: I mean, there is almost no topic of interest that he doesn't discuss, and I commend his Twitter account massively to you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几乎没有他不讨论的感兴趣的话题，我强烈向你们推荐他的推特账号。

sentences.en: But I also commend massively to you a book that's just come out that I read last year in manuscript,
sentences.zh: 但我还要强烈向你们推荐一本刚出版的书，我去年读过它的手稿，

sentences.en: and it's called Magic in Merlin's Realm, A History of Occult Politics in Britain.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《梅林的领域：英国神秘政治史》。

sentences.en: So the theme of the book is very much the occult use that rulers in Britain have made.
sentences.zh: 这本书的主题很大程度上是关于英国统治者对神秘学的使用。

sentences.en: It's completely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: In fact, do you know what I said about it?
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道我怎么评价它吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to know what I said about it?
sentences.zh: 你想知道我怎么评价它吗？

sentences.en: Did you say it was sacral?
sentences.zh: 你说它是神圣的吗？

sentences.en: No, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: I said it was learned, judicious, and rich in entertaining detail.
sentences.zh: 我说它博学、审慎，且充满了有趣的细节。

sentences.en: And I haven't enjoyed a history book this much in ages.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没有这么喜欢一本历史书了。

sentences.en: Probably not since you read my last book, Tom.
sentences.zh: 大概自从你读了我上一本书之后吧，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it's up there with yours.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，它和你的书一样好。

sentences.en: Francis, thanks so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，非常感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: You call your book, well, no, actually, first of all, in reply to Dominic's thing, do you know about sunflower seeds?
sentences.zh: 你把你的书称为，嗯，不，实际上，首先，针对多米尼克的问题，你知道向日葵种子的事吗？

sentences.en: Is this a thing?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I know the political significance of sunflower seeds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道向日葵种子的政治意义。

sentences.en: I'm not aware of any occult or magical significance to them, although it seems that magical practitioners are giving them their own new significance as we speak.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它们有什么神秘或魔法意义，尽管看起来魔法从业者们正在赋予它们新的意义。

sentences.en: And I guess that that's how magic works, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这就是魔法运作的方式，不是吗？

sentences.en: That you kind of adopt things and then weave it into your spells or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你采纳一些东西，然后把它编织进你的咒语或其他什么东西里。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: It's kind of chaotic, but it also has its own internal logic, which may not seem very logical to anyone who's from a sort of Western scientific rational background.
sentences.zh: 它有点混乱，但也有其内在逻辑，对于那些来自西方科学理性背景的人来说，这可能看起来不太合逻辑。

sentences.en: But certainly, yeah, magic makes use of things for a reason always.
sentences.zh: 但当然，是的，魔法总是出于某种原因利用事物。

sentences.en: If we roll back the years, you've called your book Merlin's Realm.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回顾过去，你把你的书命名为《梅林的领域》。

sentences.en: And Merlin is probably, well, not just in Britain, I mean, globally, perhaps, the most famous magician to have advised a king.
sentences.zh: 梅林可能是，嗯，不仅在英国，在全球范围内，也许是为国王提供建议的最著名的魔法师。

sentences.en: Where do these traditions about Merlin as King Arthur's advisor, where do they come from?
sentences.zh: 关于梅林作为亚瑟王顾问的这些传统，它们来自哪里？

sentences.en: Well, they go back really to one key figure, who's Geoffrey of Monmouth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们确实可以追溯到一个关键人物，即蒙茅斯的杰弗里。

sentences.en: And Geoffrey of Monmouth in the 12th century elaborates all sorts of extraordinary legends about fictitious or semi-fictitious British kings.
sentences.zh: 蒙茅斯的杰弗里在12世纪阐述了各种关于虚构或半虚构英国国王的非凡传说。

sentences.en: And the one who's really stuck and stood the test of time is, of course, King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 而那个真正留下来并经受住时间考验的，当然是亚瑟王。

sentences.en: And accompanying him, his magical advisor, Merlin.
sentences.zh: 以及陪伴他的魔法顾问梅林。

sentences.en: Although it's interesting that Geoffrey never actually uses words to describe Merlin that are specifically about magic.
sentences.zh: 尽管有趣的是，杰弗里从未用过专门描述魔法的词汇来描述梅林。

sentences.en: He never calls him a wizard or a magus or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 他从不称他为巫师、法师或类似的东西。

sentences.en: He's more presented as a cunning artificer, as an advisor, as a craftsman, as somebody who's a master of technology and secret wisdom.
sentences.zh: 他更多地被呈现为一位狡黠的工匠、顾问、手艺人，一个精通技术和秘密智慧的人。

sentences.en: Because he brings Stonehenge, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他带来了巨石阵，不是吗？

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So that's his signature achievement.
sentences.zh: 所以那是他的标志性成就。

sentences.en: He's managing to move Stonehenge from Ireland to bring it to Britain.
sentences.zh: 他设法将巨石阵从爱尔兰搬到了英国。

sentences.en: But yes, I mean, the figure of Merlin is older.
sentences.zh: 但是的，我的意思是，梅林的形象更古老。

sentences.en: He does go before – we do find him in earlier sources before Geoffrey of Monmouth.
sentences.zh: 他确实存在于更早的来源中，在蒙茅斯的杰弗里之前。

sentences.en: But what Geoffrey does is he brings together these two different characters, one of whom is Mervyn Wicht,
sentences.zh: 但杰弗里所做的是将这两个不同的人物结合在一起，其中一个是默文·威奇特（Mervyn Wicht），

sentences.en: who is this kind of wild man of the woods figure, who is the bard of King Gwenvolu.
sentences.zh: 他是那种森林里的野人形象，是格温沃卢国王的吟游诗人。

sentences.en: And at a battle in the 6th century, the Battle of Arthoret, Mervyn goes mad and he hides in the woods.
sentences.zh: 在6世纪的一场战役，阿索雷特战役中，默文发疯并躲进了森林。

sentences.en: And he becomes a wild man, a bit like King Nebuchadnezzar.
sentences.zh: 他变成了一个野人，有点像尼布甲尼撒国王。

sentences.en: He sort of lives as an animal.
sentences.zh: 他像动物一样生活。

sentences.en: And by living as an animal, he acquires wisdom, acquires occult knowledge and becomes a great wizard as a result of this.
sentences.zh: 通过像动物一样生活，他获得了智慧，获得了神秘知识，并因此成为了一位伟大的巫师。

sentences.en: And then the other figure is Merlin Ambrosius, who is originally from the Historia Bratonum of Nennius, which is a sort of early medieval Welsh narrative.
sentences.zh: 另一个人物是梅林·安布罗修斯，他最初来自内尼乌斯的《不列颠史》，那是一种中世纪早期的威尔士叙事。

sentences.en: And Ambrosius is a boy who manages to solve King Vortigern's problem where his castle in Carmarthen is being undermined by these two dragons,
sentences.zh: 安布罗修斯是一个男孩，他设法解决了沃蒂根国王的问题，当时他的卡马森城堡正被两条龙破坏，

sentences.en: one red and one white, who are fighting each other.
sentences.zh: 一条红色的和一条白色的，它们正在互相争斗。

sentences.en: And Ambrosius gives the interpretation and says, well, one of these dragons, the red one represents the Britons and the white one represents the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 安布罗修斯给出了诠释，说，嗯，其中一条龙，红色的代表不列颠人，白色的代表撒克逊人。

sentences.en: And essentially, this is a parable about the state of Britain at this point.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这是一个关于当时英国状况的寓言。

sentences.en: And so what Geoffrey does is he says, well, actually, these are both the same person.
sentences.zh: 所以杰弗里所做的是，他说，嗯，实际上，这两个人是同一个人。

sentences.en: But essentially, he invents Merlin as a new figure.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，他发明了梅林作为一个新人物。

sentences.en: Merlin is a confection, if not necessarily a complete creation of Geoffrey of Monmouth.
sentences.zh: 梅林是一个拼凑物，如果不是蒙茅斯的杰弗里完全创造的话。

sentences.en: Going into sort of moving slightly forward, sort of medieval period, the idea of the king having a sort of wise counsellor, an artificer, somebody who had secret knowledge.
sentences.zh: 稍微向前推进一点，进入中世纪时期，国王拥有某种明智的顾问、工匠、拥有秘密知识的人的想法。

sentences.en: Was that something, do you think, that by and large, I mean, because obviously,
sentences.zh: 你认为这在很大程度上是某种东西吗，我的意思是，因为显然，

sentences.en: when I think about some of the characters we've talked about in this podcast over the sort of the span of the centuries,
sentences.zh: 当我想到我们在本播客中讨论过的一些人物，跨越了几个世纪，

sentences.en: or I don't know, Charlemagne had, you know, learned people, scholars, at his court, Alcuin of York, very famously.
sentences.zh: 或者我不知道，查理曼大帝在宫廷里有博学的人、学者，比如著名的约克的阿尔昆。

sentences.en: Was that a sort of part of the formula, would you say, of kind of medieval kingship, that you had to have your own Merlin figure?
sentences.zh: 你会说这是中世纪王权公式的一部分吗，即你必须拥有自己的梅林式人物？

sentences.en: Yes, I think it was.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly every medieval monarch, Christian medieval monarch, or indeed Muslim medieval monarch,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然每一位中世纪君主，基督教中世纪君主，或者确实是穆斯林中世纪君主，

sentences.en: would have consciously modelled himself, had to consciously modelled himself, on that most splendid of all biblical kings, Solomon.
sentences.zh: 都会自觉地模仿，必须自觉地模仿那位最辉煌的圣经国王——所罗门。

sentences.en: And while Solomon was renowned for his splendour, for his building projects, for his wealth, he was also renowned for his mastery of occult wisdom and his command over spirits.
sentences.zh: 虽然所罗门以其辉煌、建筑项目和财富而闻名，但他还以精通神秘智慧和对灵魂的掌控而闻名。

sentences.en: And you find lots of apocryphal works, you know, both Christian, Jewish and Islamic, that talk about Solomon's mastery of the occult.
sentences.zh: 你会发现许多伪经作品，你知道，无论是基督教、犹太教还是伊斯兰教的，都在谈论所罗门对神秘学的掌控。

sentences.en: So as soon as you're going into the realms of royal splendour, fantasy royal splendour, the kind of things that kings long for, they will immediately fix on that figure of Solomon.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你进入皇家辉煌、幻想皇家辉煌的领域，即国王们渴望的那种东西，他们就会立即锁定所罗门这个形象。

sentences.en: And therefore, magic is not far behind.
sentences.zh: 因此，魔法也就紧随其后了。

sentences.en: But Francis, there's a difference, isn't there, between learned churchmen, who are schooled in the wisdom of the Bible and the church fathers and so on,
sentences.zh: 但是弗朗西斯，这有区别，不是吗，在受过圣经和教会神父智慧教育的博学教士，

sentences.en: and a figure like Merlin, who is invoking occult powers, looking at the future.
sentences.zh: 和一个像梅林这样调用神秘力量、预见未来的人物之间？

sentences.en: He's more starker and more dangerous, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他更严厉、更危险，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, in some traditions, he's the son of the devil, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些传统中，他是魔鬼的儿子，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, Merlin is a very interesting figure, and in some ways a unique figure.
sentences.zh: 是的，梅林是一个非常有趣的人物，在某些方面是一个独特的人物。

sentences.en: Because unlike a normal human magician, as understood in the Middle Ages,
sentences.zh: 因为与中世纪理解的普通人类魔法师不同，

sentences.en: Merlin doesn't actually need to invoke anyone, because Merlin is, as you say, the son of an incubus.
sentences.zh: 梅林实际上不需要召唤任何人，因为梅林正如你所说，是一个梦魇的儿子。

sentences.en: So in other words, he's the result of a plan to create the Antichrist gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他是创造敌基督计划失败的结果。

sentences.en: So according to Geoffrey...
sentences.zh: 所以根据杰弗里的说法……

sentences.en: So a useful guy to have around.
sentences.zh: 所以是一个很有用的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: How could that plan go right?
sentences.zh: 那个计划怎么会成功呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, essentially, the devil wanted to create the Antichrist and wanted to father the Antichrist on the nun, who was Merlin's mother.
sentences.zh: 是的，本质上，魔鬼想创造敌基督，并想让敌基督成为梅林母亲（一位修女）的孩子。

sentences.en: But it so happens that Merlin grew up to not be the AntichriSt.
sentences.zh: 但碰巧梅林长大后并没有成为敌基督。

sentences.en: And so he's got all the powers that the Antichrist ought to have, but he's actually not evil.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有敌基督应该拥有的所有力量，但他实际上并不邪恶。

sentences.en: So he is this absolutely unique figure.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个绝对独特的人物。

sentences.en: Massive disappointment to his father.
sentences.zh: 对他父亲来说是个巨大的失望。

sentences.en: Great shame.
sentences.zh: 真是遗憾。

sentences.en: And he can look into the future as well.
sentences.zh: 而且他也能预见未来。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the other key thing, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是另一个关键点，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, he's kind of like a think tank or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他有点像智库之类的东西。

sentences.en: Telling the government what's going to happen in the future.
sentences.zh: 告诉政府未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Yes, and prophecy is absolutely key to medieval politics.
sentences.zh: 是的，预言对于中世纪政治绝对是关键。

sentences.en: Prophecy, both popular prophecy, things that are rallying rebellions and inspiring popular revolts, but also prophecies that kings and queens themselves are listening to.
sentences.zh: 预言，既有大众预言，即那些煽动叛乱和激发民众起义的东西，也有国王和王后们自己听取的预言。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, Merlin has this reputation very much as a prophet to the point that I would say in the Middle Ages, Merlin is more renowned as a prophet.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，梅林确实有作为先知的声誉，以至于我会说在中世纪，梅林作为先知更出名。

sentences.en: He's more of a kind of Nostradamus type figure than he is a wizard, a kind of Harry Potter type figure.
sentences.zh: 他更像是一个诺查丹玛斯式的人物，而不是一个巫师，一个哈利·波特式的人物。

sentences.en: You know, the prophecy aspect is very much to the thought.
sentences.zh: 你知道，预言方面非常突出。

sentences.en: And Francis, so let's say Plantagenet, England.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，那么，假设是金雀花王朝的英格兰。

sentences.en: Do people think Merlin was a genuine historical figure, that he genuinely absolutely existed?
sentences.zh: 人们认为梅林是一个真实的历史人物，他确实绝对存在吗？

sentences.en: Or do they approach the sort of Geoffrey and Monmouth stuff and the sort of legends that are circulating a bit more?
sentences.zh: 还是他们以更批判的方式对待蒙茅斯的杰弗里的东西和流传的传说？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, are they approaching them critically or literally?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他们是批判性地还是字面地对待它们？

sentences.en: Well, it's not until the 17th century that Merlin's historical existence is actually questioned by historians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，直到17世纪，梅林的历史存在才真正受到历史学家的质疑。

sentences.en: So, yes, I mean, he is essentially accepted as being a historical character, whilst at the same time, he was also a literary character.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我的意思是，他基本上被接受为一个历史人物，同时他也是一个文学人物。

sentences.en: So I suppose he's a figure who has multiple different existences in different genres.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他是一个在不同体裁中拥有多种不同存在的人物。

sentences.en: But certainly the idea that Merlin was a King Arthur's advisor, that he had foretold and made accurate prophecies, was something that, yeah,
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，梅林是亚瑟王的顾问，他预言并做出了准确的预言，这在金雀花王朝的英格兰，

sentences.en: people would have taken literally as historically true in Plantagenet, England.
sentences.zh: 人们会字面地将其视为历史事实。

sentences.en: And so why is Merlin appearing in the form that he takes when he does?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么梅林会以他出现时的那种形式出现呢？

sentences.en: So in your book, you say that, as far as you know, the first example of a king using occult powers for political ends is William the Conqueror, trying to take down Heroid the Wake,
sentences.zh: 所以你在书中说，据你所知，国王利用神秘力量达到政治目的的第一个例子是威廉征服者，试图打倒赫里沃德（Heroid the Wake），

sentences.en: who is holed up in the marshes around Ely.
sentences.zh: 他躲在伊利周围的沼泽地里。

sentences.en: And he gets, you don't call her a witch, but she's someone who can invoke kind of powers.
sentences.zh: 他找了一个人，你没称她为女巫，但她是一个能调用某种力量的人。

sentences.en: And that all goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 结果一切都搞砸了。

sentences.en: I've got a good fact for you.
sentences.zh: 我有一个关于你的好事实。

sentences.en: I've got a brilliant fact for you.
sentences.zh: 我有一个关于你的精彩事实。

sentences.en: Heroid the Wake's descendant is a listener to this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 赫里沃德的后代是这个播客的听众。

sentences.en: Oh, well, that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, because Heroid the Wake defeats this occult practitioner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为赫里沃德打败了这个神秘学从业者。

sentences.en: So he or she will be very happy to hear that.
sentences.zh: 所以他或她会很高兴听到这个消息。

sentences.en: Francis, why is William the Conqueror and his heirs kind of buying into this stuff in what seems to be a new way?
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，为什么威廉征服者和他的继承人会以一种似乎是全新的方式接受这些东西？

sentences.en: Well, the reason why Merlin comes along at the moment that he does, I've argued, is because in the 12th century, so a little bit after William the Conqueror,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我论证过，梅林之所以在那个时刻出现，是因为在12世纪，也就是威廉征服者之后不久，

sentences.en: you've got this sudden influx of new knowledge that's coming into Western Europe and coming into Britain.
sentences.zh: 一股新的知识浪潮正涌入西欧，并传入英国。

sentences.en: And this is new knowledge from the Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 这些新知识源自伊斯兰世界。

sentences.en: So you've got astrology, so you've got astrology, alchemy, various different forms of divination,
sentences.zh: 所以你有了占星术、炼金术，以及各种形式的占卜，

sentences.en: these forms of knowledge that have huge potential to expand our ability to predict the future.
sentences.zh: 这些知识形式蕴含着巨大的潜力，能增强我们预测未来的能力。

sentences.en: So people believe, but they also contain within them tremendous danger.
sentences.zh: 人们对此深信不疑，但这些知识同时也潜藏着巨大的危险。

sentences.en: And so it's almost like these are disruptive spiritual technologies.
sentences.zh: 所以，这几乎就像是某种颠覆性的精神技术。

sentences.en: I suppose you could think of them as being that are coming in there and potentially upending everything that people thought they were certain of with regard to politics.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以把它们看作是某种外来事物，它们可能会颠覆人们在政治方面自以为确信的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, when you look at the Anglo-Saxon period, the only form of political prophecy really took place through brontology,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你审视盎格鲁-撒克逊时期，唯一的政治预言形式其实是通过雷占术进行的，

sentences.en: and that was attempting to predict the future through the sound of thunder.
sentences.zh: 也就是试图通过雷声来预测未来。

sentences.en: There wasn't a practice of astrology.
sentences.zh: 当时并没有占星术的实践。

sentences.en: There wasn't a practice of alchemy.
sentences.zh: 也没有炼金术的实践。

sentences.en: But these new techniques coming from the Greek world, from the Islamic world, from the East, from the South,
sentences.zh: 但这些来自希腊世界、伊斯兰世界、东方和南方的新技术，

sentences.en: they come into Britain and they need a figure who somehow makes sense of them.
sentences.zh: 它们传入英国后，需要一个人物来以某种方式解读它们。

sentences.en: Is that because they can't be nakedly, say, Islamic or from Byzantium?
sentences.zh: 这是因为它们不能赤裸裸地说是伊斯兰教的，或者来自拜占庭吗？

sentences.en: Because then they would just seem weird and foreign.
sentences.zh: 因为那样的话，它们看起来会显得怪异且陌生。

sentences.en: But if you can repackage them as kind of primordially British.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能把它们重新包装成某种原始的英国本土产物呢？

sentences.en: But also, surely, Tom, they're a threat to the – if you say there's these brilliant ideas coming from the Islamic world,
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，这肯定也构成了威胁——如果你说这些绝妙的想法来自伊斯兰世界，

sentences.en: isn't that a threat to the sort of implicit monopoly of the Christian church in Britain?
sentences.zh: 这难道不对英国基督教会的某种隐性垄断构成威胁吗？

sentences.en: Do you not think to acknowledge that there's a civilization with a really, as Francis says, a technologically sophisticated set of skills, a very particular set of skills, Tom,
sentences.zh: 难道你不认为，承认存在一个像弗朗西斯所说的那样，拥有一套技术精湛的技能、一套非常特殊的技能的文明，汤姆，

sentences.en: as you know from your Liam Neeson impersonation, a very particular set of skills that they don't have – the Archbishop of Canterbury doesn't have.
sentences.zh: 正如你从你模仿连姆·尼森的表演中所知道的那样，一套他们所不具备的、坎特伯雷大主教也不具备的非常特殊的技能，

sentences.en: So they have to package it in Merlin.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须把这一切包装在梅林身上。

sentences.en: Is that basically it, Francis?
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，基本情况就是这样吗？

sentences.en: It's a little bit of both, really, because on the one hand, there is this belief that if something is new and if something is powerful,
sentences.zh: 其实两者兼而有之，因为一方面，人们相信如果某样东西是新的且强大的，

sentences.en: then an exotic connection with the Islamic world, with the Jewish world is desirable, because that kind of gives it that feeling that it's something different, new and powerful.
sentences.zh: 那么与伊斯兰世界、犹太世界建立某种异域联系是令人向往的，因为这赋予了它一种与众不同、新颖且强大的感觉。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, as you say, there is this feeling of pride that, you know, we don't want to admit that there's another civilization better than us.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，正如你所说，存在一种自豪感，你知道，我们不想承认有另一个文明比我们更优秀。

sentences.en: And so you get stories being elaborated, like the idea that Merlin actually learnt alchemy, went to Toledo and learnt alchemy from the masters of Toledo,
sentences.zh: 于是就有了各种编造的故事，比如梅林实际上学习了炼金术，去了托莱多，并从托莱多的大师那里学到了炼金术，

sentences.en: or indeed that Merlin invented alchemy in Britain and actually exported alchemy to the Islamic world and taught it to them, which is a bit like, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者甚至说梅林在英国发明了炼金术，并将其出口到伊斯兰世界传授给他们，这有点像，你知道，

sentences.en: the idea that King Arthur conquered Rome and all these, you know, wild stories that appear in medieval literature.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟王征服罗马之类的想法，以及中世纪文学中出现的那些荒诞故事。

sentences.en: So, Francis, in that case, I mean, Merlin becomes a very popular figure, not just in Britain, but across Europe.
sentences.zh: 那么，弗朗西斯，在这种情况下，梅林不仅在英国，而且在整个欧洲都成为了一个非常受欢迎的人物。

sentences.en: And so does his fame then serve to cast Britain as a natural home of magic?
sentences.zh: 那么他的名声是否起到了将英国塑造为魔法天然家园的作用？

sentences.en: And the English kings, I guess, particularly, do they come to see themselves as, you know, the heirs of this tradition,
sentences.zh: 我想，英国国王们，特别是他们，是否开始将自己视为这一传统的继承者，

sentences.en: and therefore this gives them a license to explore this alchemical occult stuff?
sentences.zh: 并因此获得了探索这些炼金术和神秘学事物的许可？

sentences.en: Oh, very much so, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: I would say that Merlin's status as British is quite critical, even though, as you say, his fame spreads well beyond Britain.
sentences.zh: 我想说，梅林作为英国人的身份至关重要，尽管正如你所说，他的名声远播至英国之外。

sentences.en: Bear in mind that when we talk about Merlin as a British figure, we mean that in the broadest possible sense, not just that he is connected with the island of Britain,
sentences.zh: 请记住，当我们谈论梅林作为英国人物时，我们是在最广泛的意义上理解的，不仅仅是他与不列颠岛有关，

sentences.en: but he's also connected with the British people, who are more widely dispersed than that as a result of the migration in late antiquity of British people to Brittany,
sentences.zh: 他还与英国人民有关，由于古代晚期英国人向布列塔尼的迁徙，他们分布得更广，

sentences.en: and indeed to parts of northern Spain.
sentences.zh: 甚至延伸到了西班牙北部的一些地区。

sentences.en: And so you've got this permeation of British culture into French courtly culture at a very early era.
sentences.zh: 所以，英国文化在很早的时期就渗透到了法国宫廷文化中。

sentences.en: And so from a very early period, Merlin becomes a crucial character in that French courtly literature.
sentences.zh: 因此，从很早开始，梅林就成为了法国宫廷文学中的关键角色。

sentences.en: And yes, he is always connected to Britain.
sentences.zh: 是的，他总是与英国联系在一起。

sentences.en: And that connection between Britain and magic goes way back.
sentences.zh: 而英国与魔法之间的那种联系由来已久。

sentences.en: I mean, we find, you know, Pliny the Elder writing about how, you know, Britain excels the Persians in its magic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们发现老普林尼写道，英国的魔法胜过波斯。

sentences.en: So proud.
sentences.zh: 真令人自豪。

sentences.en: I hope Ali Ansari is listening to this.
sentences.zh: 我希望阿里·安萨里正在听这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I mean, you yourself, Tom, will know about the megaliths and the importance that they hold, you know, as a source of this impression of magic about Britain,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，汤姆，你自己也会了解巨石阵及其重要性，你知道，它们是英国魔法印象的来源，

sentences.en: these mysterious buildings.
sentences.zh: 这些神秘的建筑。

sentences.en: And, you know, even the Romans were aware, even the Greeks perhaps were aware that Britain contained these strange monuments in Wiltshire, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，甚至罗马人也意识到，甚至希腊人也许也意识到，英国在威尔特郡拥有这些奇怪的纪念碑，你知道，

sentences.en: that were the work of giants or the work of magicians.
sentences.zh: 它们是巨人的杰作，或者是魔法师的杰作。

sentences.en: And therefore, that's something which, you know, Britain very much from an early date gets this reputation as a shadowy island, you know, shaded in mist, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是为什么英国很早就获得了这种阴暗岛屿的声誉，你知道，笼罩在迷雾中，你知道，

sentences.en: is home to druids and wizards and so forth.
sentences.zh: 是德鲁伊、巫师等等的家园。

sentences.en: So Merlin very much ties into that classical tradition of Britain as a mystical place.
sentences.zh: 所以梅林与英国作为神秘之地的古典传统紧密相连。

sentences.en: Before Tom starts talking about Wiltshire, which we absolutely must avoid for answers at all costs, I think we should move the story on a tiny bit.
sentences.zh: 在汤姆开始谈论威尔特郡之前——我们绝对必须不惜一切代价避免在回答中提到它——我认为我们应该把故事稍微推进一点。

sentences.en: And definitely we don't want to get into Pliny the Elder, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而且我们绝对不想深入探讨老普林尼，汤姆。

sentences.en: So harsh.
sentences.zh: 太刻薄了。

sentences.en: It's tough love in this podcast today.
sentences.zh: 今天的播客真是严厉的爱。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So let's talk about sort of real, as it were, people.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们谈谈所谓的“真实”的人吧。

sentences.en: I'm not dissing Merlin, but who would you say is…
sentences.zh: 我不是在贬低梅林，但你会说谁是……

sentences.en: Well, you absolutely are.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你绝对是在贬低他。

sentences.en: I'm saying he's got multiple selves, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我是说他有多个自我，汤姆。

sentences.en: Let's talk about people who are mono-selfed.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈那些“单一自我”的人吧。

sentences.en: So who's the first, as it were, occult figure who you think really matters in terms of kind of, let's say, English royal politics?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为在英国王室政治方面，第一个真正重要的神秘学人物是谁？

sentences.en: Well, I think the first real world person that we encounter who is willing to kind of take on this mantle of Merlin and become a Merlin to a real king is Roger Bacon,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们遇到的第一个愿意承担起梅林这一角色，并成为现实中国王的“梅林”的真实人物是罗杰·培根，

sentences.en: the great Franciscan scientist of the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 13世纪伟大的方济各会科学家。

sentences.en: And he begins to advise Henry III, begins to write treatises on occult topics that are dedicated to Henry.
sentences.zh: 他开始为亨利三世提供建议，并开始撰写献给亨利的神秘学著作。

sentences.en: Michael Scott is another figure, although in his case, he leaves Scotland, his land of his birth, and ends up working for the court of the Holy Roman Emperor in Sicily.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·斯科特是另一个人，尽管在他那个例子中，他离开了出生地苏格兰，最终为西西里岛的神圣罗马帝国皇帝效力。

sentences.en: But again, you know, he's somebody who has a tremendous magical reputation, although in both cases,
sentences.zh: 但同样，你知道，他也是一个拥有巨大魔法声誉的人，尽管在这两个例子中，

sentences.en: their magical reputation is rather exaggerated and elaborated after their deaths.
sentences.zh: 他们的魔法声誉在死后都被相当夸大和润色了。

sentences.en: So you have to be quite careful in separating truth from fiction when it comes to a lot of these characters.
sentences.zh: 所以当谈到这些人物时，你必须非常小心地将事实与虚构区分开来。

sentences.en: And so Roger Bacon is working with Henry III principally.
sentences.zh: 所以罗杰·培根主要是与亨利三世合作。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so Henry III is obviously very interested in this.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利三世显然对此非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And you talk about how there's a weird sacral tiling in Westminster Abbey designed to invoke the legacy of Solomon and all that kind of stuff, which is still there, right?
sentences.zh: 你谈到威斯敏斯特教堂里有一种奇怪的圣像瓷砖，旨在援引所罗门的遗产等等，这些东西现在还在那里，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, so when the coronation of Charles III, he'll be sitting on a Solomonic occult piece of tiling dating back to the time of Roger Bacon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当查尔斯三世加冕时，他将坐在一块可以追溯到罗杰·培根时代的所罗门神秘瓷砖上。

sentences.en: Would that be right?
sentences.zh: 这样说对吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's recently been restored in the last decade or so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它在过去十年左右的时间里刚刚被修复。

sentences.en: And for Elizabeth II's coronation, it was covered up by a carpet, as it had been for a long time, because it had got, you know, really, it was in a state.
sentences.zh: 在伊丽莎白二世加冕时，它被地毯覆盖着，就像它长期以来那样，因为它当时的状态真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: But it's a Cosmati pavement.
sentences.zh: 但那是一块科斯马蒂路面。

sentences.en: So using that wonderful technique that's popular in medieval Italy, where it's a little bit like mosaic,
sentences.zh: 所以使用了那种在中世纪意大利很流行的奇妙技术，它有点像马赛克，

sentences.en: but you use marble and glass and all sorts of bits and pieces of different sizes to create these extraordinary patterns.
sentences.zh: 但你使用大理石、玻璃以及各种不同尺寸的碎片来创造这些非凡的图案。

sentences.en: And the one in Westminster Abbey was created by the monks.
sentences.zh: 威斯敏斯特教堂的那一块是由僧侣们创造的。

sentences.en: And quite explicitly, it represents a microcosm of the world.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常明确地代表了世界的缩影。

sentences.en: And this idea of as above, so below, we find in the writings attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, the idea that the world that we inhabit is a microcosmos,
sentences.zh: 这种“如其在上，如其在下”的思想，我们在归于赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯的著作中发现，即我们居住的世界是一个小宇宙，

sentences.en: is a smaller version of the great world, the spiritual world, the macrocosm of the planets, the universe, and God and the angels.
sentences.zh: 是宏大的世界、精神世界、行星、宇宙、上帝和天使的大宇宙的较小版本。

sentences.en: And so if we create the right images that mirror that macrocosm of the spiritual world, then we can draw down those spiritual powers and rays from the cosmos.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们创造出能够映射那个精神世界大宇宙的正确图像，我们就能从宇宙中汲取那些精神力量和射线。

sentences.en: And that's essentially what this is.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: It's a kind of machine of empowerment.
sentences.zh: 它是一种赋能机器。

sentences.en: When the king sits on top of this Cosmati pavement at the right moment,
sentences.zh: 当国王在适当的时候坐在这一科斯马蒂路面上时，

sentences.en: because coronations were almost always scheduled astrologically to ensure that they took place at the most propitious time,
sentences.zh: 因为加冕典礼几乎总是按占星术安排，以确保它们在最有利的时间举行，

sentences.en: then those rays will enter the body of the king and will empower the king to be this semi-divine figure.
sentences.zh: 那么这些射线就会进入国王的身体，并赋予国王成为这种半神人物的力量。

sentences.en: So, yes, it is quite literally a magical process.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这确实是一个魔法过程。

sentences.en: Prince Charles is going to love that.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯王子会喜欢这个的。

sentences.en: I mean, I thought he was really, really into that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我以为他真的非常沉迷于那种东西。

sentences.en: And so then after Henry III, the medieval English king who really is into the occult is Richard II.
sentences.zh: 那么在亨利三世之后，真正沉迷于神秘学的中世纪英国国王是理查二世。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And he's a bit too into it.
sentences.zh: 而且他沉迷得有点过头了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in what sense is he too into it?
sentences.zh: 那么他在什么意义上沉迷得过头了？

sentences.en: Well, Richard II, as I'm sure any of your listeners who are into medieval history will know, was not a wildly successful king.
sentences.zh: 嗯，理查二世，我相信你们任何对中世纪历史感兴趣的听众都知道，他并不是一位非常成功的国王。

sentences.en: He ends up being deposed and dying horribly by his relative, Henry Bolingbroke, who becomes Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 他最终被他的亲戚亨利·博林布鲁克（即后来的亨利四世）废黜并惨死。

sentences.en: And really his reign unwinds as a result of his over-reliance on his occult beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他的统治实际上是因为他过度依赖自己的神秘学信仰而瓦解的。

sentences.en: So he comes to believe his own propaganda, if you like, about himself as this kind of mystical world emperor who will bring world peace and bring an end to all strife.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始相信自己的宣传，如果你愿意的话，相信自己是那种能带来世界和平并终结所有纷争的神秘世界皇帝。

sentences.en: He's John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 他是约翰·列侬。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: But the trouble is, something I talk about in the book is the danger of magical quietism.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，我在书中谈到过魔法静默主义的危险。

sentences.en: So if you're a ruler who really believes this stuff, if you become almost addicted to prophecy or divination, then you will stop acting in the real world.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一位真正相信这些东西的统治者，如果你变得几乎沉迷于预言或占卜，那么你就会停止在现实世界中采取行动。

sentences.en: You'll actually stop taking the measures that you need to actually preserve your power.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会停止采取那些你需要采取的、真正能够维护你权力的措施。

sentences.en: And you will become divorced from the real world, shed your pragmatism and sort of live in a land of fantasy, which perhaps we could see in certain world leaders today,
sentences.zh: 你会变得与现实世界脱节，抛弃你的务实精神，生活在幻想的世界里，这也许我们在当今某些世界领导人身上也能看到，

sentences.en: that they're more preoccupied with the legends that they have themselves have spun than they are with real world probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他们更关心自己编造的传说，而不是现实世界的问题。

sentences.en: And yeah,
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: essentially his reign unwinds because he spends more time with the soothsayers and the astrologers and the diviners than he does with his council actually plotting how he's going to stay on the throne.
sentences.zh: 他的统治本质上是因为他花在与占卜师、占星家和预言家相处的时间，比他与议会商讨如何保住王位的时间还要多而瓦解的。

sentences.en: But that's a bit like Rudolf II, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这有点像鲁道夫二世，不是吗？

sentences.en: In Prague or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在布拉格之类的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a common, I mean, I know they're centuries apart, but is this, do you think, Francis, I get the impression you think this is a common hazard?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很常见，我的意思是，我知道他们相隔几个世纪，但弗朗西斯，你认为这是一种常见的危险吗？

sentences.en: That if you're surrounded by conjurers and stuff, then it's a sort of repeating formula, is it?
sentences.zh: 如果你被术士之类的人包围，那么这是一种重复的模式，是吗？

sentences.en: That monarchs start thinking too much about the alignment of the planets and not enough about, you know, bread and taxes and stuff?
sentences.zh: 君主们开始过多地考虑行星的排列，而没有足够地考虑面包、税收之类的东西？

sentences.en: Yes, it is a danger that more than one monarch has fallen into.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是不止一位君主陷入过的危险。

sentences.en: Perhaps the most famous example in modern times would be Nicholas II and the sway that Rasputin managed to gain over him, even in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 现代最著名的例子可能就是尼古拉二世，以及拉斯普京甚至在20世纪都能对他施加的影响。

sentences.en: So yes, there are plenty of examples from throughout the world of monarchs who've fallen into this trap.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，世界各地有许多君主陷入这个陷阱的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also there's the classic story of the misinterpreting a sign because he, Richard II, is told to beware of toads, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个经典的误解征兆的故事，因为理查二世被告知要提防蟾蜍，不是吗？

sentences.en: That toads will overthrow him.
sentences.zh: 说蟾蜍会推翻他。

sentences.en: So what does he do?
sentences.zh: 那么他做了什么？

sentences.en: Go around killing all the toads?
sentences.zh: 到处去杀蟾蜍？

sentences.en: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: And then he sees Bolingbroke wearing robes with toads on them.
sentences.zh: 然后他看到博林布鲁克穿着绣有蟾蜍的长袍。

sentences.en: Is that story actually true?
sentences.zh: 那个故事是真的吗？

sentences.en: Please tell me it is.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我它是真的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he has this fear of toads, which, of course, he interprets as being the animal, which is fair enough,
sentences.zh: 所以他有一种对蟾蜍的恐惧，当然，他将其解读为那种动物，这很合理，

sentences.en: because toads have this strong association in medieval myth with poison and the belief that toads are poisonous and that, you know, poison can be made from the toad.
sentences.zh: 因为蟾蜍在中世纪神话中与毒药有很强的联系，人们相信蟾蜍是有毒的，而且你知道，毒药可以用蟾蜍制成。

sentences.en: There was a belief that King John, for example, had been killed by the poison of a toad.
sentences.zh: 有一种说法是，例如，约翰王就是被蟾蜍的毒液杀死的。

sentences.en: But what Richard II does is he sends Henry Bolingbroke into exile.
sentences.zh: 但理查二世所做的是将亨利·博林布鲁克流放。

sentences.en: And on the day that Bolingbroke comes back from exile, he comes into the court wearing this robe that's richly embroidered with green toads.
sentences.zh: 而在博林布鲁克从流放中回来的那天，他穿着一件绣满绿色蟾蜍的长袍进入宫廷。

sentences.en: But, of course, by that time, it's too late.
sentences.zh: 但当然，到那时已经太晚了。

sentences.en: Bolingbroke has re-established his power base.
sentences.zh: 博林布鲁克已经重建了他的权力基础。

sentences.en: He's come back from exile.
sentences.zh: 他已经从流放中回来了。

sentences.en: And, yeah, Richard has misinterpreted the sign.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，理查误解了这个征兆。

sentences.en: So it's very Macbeth, kind of being given prophecies that then trip you up.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常像《麦克白》，那种被预言所误导的感觉。

sentences.en: Francis, I think we should take a break when we come to the end of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，我想当我们进入中世纪末期时，我们应该休息一下。

sentences.en: So in the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 也就是在宗教改革时期。

sentences.en: But before we do, just looking at the fifth, the history of the 15th century where we say we did an episode on the princess in the tower.
sentences.zh: 但在我们这样做之前，看看15世纪的历史，我们说我们做了一期关于塔中王子的节目。

sentences.en: And we looked at how Richard III uses accusations of sorcery and necromancy to trip up his enemies.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了理查三世是如何利用巫术和招魂术的指控来陷害他的敌人的。

sentences.en: And that does seem to be a particular theme through the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实是15世纪的一个特定主题。

sentences.en: And I guess the most famous example of that happening is in the trial of Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 我想最著名的例子就是圣女贞德的审判。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when Joan is captured by the Burgundians and taken to the English,
sentences.zh: 所以当圣女贞德被勃艮第人俘虏并交给英国人时，

sentences.en: one of the questions is what charge should be used to discredit her and what charge should be used to justify the death penalty against her.
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是，应该用什么罪名来抹黑她，又该用什么罪名来证明对她判处死刑是正当的。

sentences.en: Now, in the end, it turns out that the main charge is heresy.
sentences.zh: 最终，主要的罪名定为异端罪。

sentences.en: But in the process, in the trial, there are those who push for the idea that she is, in fact, guilty of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但在审判过程中，有人极力主张她实际上犯有巫术罪。

sentences.en: And not only is she guilty of witchcraft, but has been using her witchcraft in order to defeat the English in battle when it should be impossible for her to do so.
sentences.zh: 而且她不仅犯有巫术罪，还利用巫术在战场上击败了英国人，而这本是不可能做到的。

sentences.en: It's the only explanation, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是唯一的解释，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The fact that she's this extraordinarily unlikely figure, a teenage girl leading an army,
sentences.zh: 事实上，她是一个极其不可思议的人物，一个十几岁的女孩带领着一支军队，

sentences.en: is turned against her and used as evidence that she must be a witch who has invoked these powers, that, you know, these voices that spoke to her,
sentences.zh: 这反而成了对她不利的证据，被用来证明她一定是个女巫，召唤了这些力量，你知道的，那些对她说话的声音，

sentences.en: these saints who appeared to her in Dom Remy, they are, in fact, devils.
sentences.zh: 那些在栋雷米向她显现的圣徒，实际上是恶魔。

sentences.en: They are demonic familiars that she has brought into her service.
sentences.zh: 它们是她招募到自己麾下的恶魔使魔。

sentences.en: And examples are used, for example, she managed to escape when she was captured at one point from a window by leaping from the window and ended up not being injured.
sentences.zh: 并且还举了例子，比如她有一次被俘时，设法从窗户跳下逃脱，结果竟然没有受伤。

sentences.en: And so that was taken as evidence that she must be protected by witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 所以这被当作她一定受到巫术保护的证据。

sentences.en: Now, in the end, the witchcraft accusation doesn't end up being used to secure the conviction.
sentences.zh: 不过，最终巫术指控并没有被用来确保定罪。

sentences.en: And the main reason for that is that it's embarrassing for the English army,
sentences.zh: 主要原因是这对英国军队来说很尴尬，

sentences.en: because if it can be shown that the English army was so weak or so ungodly that it could be defeated by the wiles of a witch, it might look bad.
sentences.zh: 因为如果能证明英国军队如此软弱或如此不虔诚，以至于被女巫的诡计击败，那看起来会很糟糕。

sentences.en: And so in the end, it comes down to the accusation of heresy and cross-dressing.
sentences.zh: 所以最后，指控还是落在了异端罪和女扮男装上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I think we should we should take a break here.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该在这里休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we will we'll get on to the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，我们将进入宗教改革的话题。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: And we are looking at occult influences on the movers and shakers of English and British history.
sentences.zh: 我们正在探讨神秘学对英国和不列颠历史进程中关键人物的影响。

sentences.en: And we've covered the Middle Ages and now we reach the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讲完了中世纪，现在来到了16世纪。

sentences.en: In Francis, the Reformation represents an absolute sea change, doesn't it, in the use that accusations of witchcraft and sorcery are put to?
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，宗教改革在巫术和妖术指控的用途上代表了一种彻底的巨变，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because essentially, Protestants accuse Catholics that this is all mumbo jumbo and mummery and sorcery.
sentences.zh: 因为本质上，新教徒指责天主教徒所做的一切都是胡言乱语、装神弄鬼和妖术。

sentences.en: And that must kind of change the terms of the debate very, very profoundly.
sentences.zh: 这必然会非常深刻地改变辩论的基调。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: It really is a sea change because in the 15th century and indeed in Henry VIII's early reign,
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场巨变，因为在15世纪，甚至在亨利八世统治初期，

sentences.en: we find accusations of witchcraft being used against the king's enemies and against political opponents of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 我们发现巫术指控被用来对付国王的敌人和各种政治对手。

sentences.en: But the idea that you could actually use this accusation in order to turn around a millennium of loyalty to the Catholic Church and the rights of the Catholic Church and convince people that their ancestral religion of Catholicism was in fact no better than a bunch of hocus pocus is an extraordinary propaganda coup.
sentences.zh: 但那种认为你可以利用这种指控来扭转对天主教会长达千年的忠诚，并说服人们他们祖传的天主教信仰实际上不过是一堆骗术，这真是一场非凡的宣传政变。

sentences.en: And it's pulled off by Thomas Cromwell, essentially, in the 1530s, with the help of propagandists like John Bale, for example, who goes to great lengths to argue that, you know,
sentences.zh: 这基本上是由托马斯·克伦威尔在16世纪30年代完成的，在像约翰·贝尔这样的宣传家的帮助下，他竭力论证，你知道的，

sentences.en: the mass is a form of sorcery and that Catholicism is witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 弥撒是一种妖术，天主教就是巫术。

sentences.en: So the mass is the key to that, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以弥撒是其中的关键，对吧？

sentences.en: The idea, the Catholics believing in transubstantiation, Protestants say that that's pure necromancy and sorcery, don't they?
sentences.zh: 天主教徒相信圣餐变体论，而新教徒说那是纯粹的招魂术和妖术，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So it's something which happens as early as the 14th century among the Lollards, you know, that dissenting group of English people who want a simpler, stripped down Christianity.
sentences.zh: 所以这早在14世纪就在罗拉德派中出现了，你知道的，那些希望基督教更简单、更纯粹的英国异见群体。

sentences.en: That's very much against the backdrop of Richard II as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上也是以理查二世为背景的，不是吗？

sentences.en: So is there a kind of link there, perhaps?
sentences.zh: 所以这之间或许有一种联系？

sentences.en: Or is it coincidence?
sentences.zh: 还是纯属巧合？

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, indirectly, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，或许是间接的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there have been lots of attempts by historians to try and see the conflict between Richard II and Henry Bolingbroke in religious terMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为历史学家们曾多次尝试从宗教角度来看待理查二世和亨利·博林布鲁克之间的冲突。

sentences.en: And it's true that Henry IV did have some Lollard servants, but on the whole, Henry himself is an anti-Lollard and in fact, Burns Lollards.
sentences.zh: 确实，亨利四世确实有一些罗拉德派的仆人，但总的来说，亨利本人是反罗拉德派的，事实上他还烧死过罗拉德派教徒。

sentences.en: So it doesn't really quite map on exactly, but certainly there's a background of turbulence in the religious sphere that is relevant.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不完全吻合，但可以肯定的是，宗教领域存在着相关的动荡背景。

sentences.en: But the Lollards had criticised transubstantiation in these terms, and they'd said transubstantiation is a doctrine of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但罗拉德派确实曾以这些术语批评过圣餐变体论，他们说圣餐变体论是一种巫术教义。

sentences.en: So we should just say that this is the idea that the body and blood, that bread and wine can literally become the body and blood of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该说明一下，这就是指身体和血，即面包和酒可以字面上变成基督的身体和血的观念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the idea that every single time a priest celebrates mass, he is performing a miracle,
sentences.zh: 所以那种认为每当牧师举行弥撒时，他就在施行奇迹的观念，

sentences.en: because the miracle is that the bread and wine are turning literally into the body and blood of Jesus.
sentences.zh: 因为奇迹在于面包和酒字面上变成了耶稣的身体和血。

sentences.en: But at the same time, they are retaining the appearance to outward sense of bread and wine.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它们在外表上仍然保留着面包和酒的样子。

sentences.en: And so that's the official doctrine of the Catholic Church.
sentences.zh: 这就是天主教会的官方教义。

sentences.en: But it's something which can be quite easily twisted in such a way that it seems like a magical doctrine.
sentences.zh: 但这很容易被扭曲，看起来像是一种魔法教义。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Protestantism beds down.
sentences.zh: 所以新教确立了下来。

sentences.en: And yet it seems odd that perhaps the single most famous figure in English history of a kind of a new Merlin, an advisor to an English king,
sentences.zh: 然而，似乎有些奇怪的是，英国历史上最著名的那种新梅林式人物，即英国国王的顾问，

sentences.en: is at the end of the 16th century to the Protestant monarch Elizabeth I, and that is Dr. John Dee.
sentences.zh: 出现在16世纪末，服务于新教君主伊丽莎白一世，那就是约翰·迪伊博士。

sentences.en: So can you tell us about him and how and why is it that in a Protestant country he is able to have the kind of reputation that he gets?
sentences.zh: 那么你能告诉我们关于他的事吗？在一个新教国家，他为何能获得那样的声誉？

sentences.en: Well, Dee is certainly the person that I'd pick out who's the most self-conscious Merlin, if you like, somebody who sees himself as being the successor to Merlin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迪伊肯定是我会挑选出的最自觉的梅林，如果你愿意这么说的话，他把自己视为梅林的继任者。

sentences.en: And I think part of that comes from the fact that the Tudor dynasty has a bit of an Arthurian complex.
sentences.zh: 我认为这部分源于都铎王朝有一种亚瑟王情结。

sentences.en: And this goes right the way back to Henry Tudor and the fact that they're a Welsh family who claim descent from Welsh princes and therefore from Arthur.
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到亨利·都铎，他们是一个威尔士家族，声称是威尔士亲王的后裔，因此也是亚瑟王的后裔。

sentences.en: Henry, of course, calls his eldest son Arthur.
sentences.zh: 亨利当然把他的长子命名为亚瑟。

sentences.en: Arthur then marries Catherine of Aragon, but doesn't live to become king, as a result of which Henry VIII succeeds.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟后来娶了阿拉贡的凯瑟琳，但没能活到继位，结果亨利八世继位了。

sentences.en: And Henry VIII has a round table constructed because he is so convinced that he is the successor of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世建造了一张圆桌，因为他深信自己是亚瑟王的继任者。

sentences.en: And when Elizabeth comes to the throne, through so many adversities, you know, so many chances there'd been for her to be executed or taken out of the line of succession,
sentences.zh: 当伊丽莎白登上王位时，经历了如此多的磨难，你知道的，她曾有那么多次机会被处决或被排除在继承权之外，

sentences.en: but she gets there in this, you know, almost miraculous way.
sentences.zh: 但她以这种近乎奇迹般的方式成功了。

sentences.en: You know, when she's told that she's going to be queen, she responds by saying, you know, it is the Lord's doing and marvellous in our eyes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当她被告知她将成为女王时，她回应说，这是上帝的作为，在我们眼中是奇妙的。

sentences.en: The implication being that it's a miracle that she ever got to that point of becoming queen.
sentences.zh: 言下之意是，她能走到成为女王这一步简直是个奇迹。

sentences.en: And she was already at that point friends with Dee.
sentences.zh: 而且她在那个时候就已经和迪伊是朋友了。

sentences.en: She's friends with Dee as Princess Elizabeth before she becomes queen.
sentences.zh: 在成为女王之前，作为伊丽莎白公主，她就和迪伊是朋友。

sentences.en: And so when she becomes queen, she occasionally relies on Dee's advice.
sentences.zh: 所以当她成为女王后，她偶尔会依赖迪伊的建议。

sentences.en: But I think that Dee himself actually exaggerates in his diaries, in his self-presentation, the extent to which he really had an influence on her.
sentences.zh: 但我认为迪伊本人实际上在他的日记和自我展示中夸大了他对她真正的影响力。

sentences.en: But even without Dee, Elizabeth is obsessed with the occult.
sentences.zh: 但即使没有迪伊，伊丽莎白也痴迷于神秘学。

sentences.en: She practices alchemy in her own free time.
sentences.zh: 她在业余时间练习炼金术。

sentences.en: Can we just talk about Dee a little bit?
sentences.zh: 我们能稍微谈谈迪伊吗？

sentences.en: Because he's such a fascinating figure.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个如此迷人的人物。

sentences.en: So he is from, he's born in, I think, London, Mortlake, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以他出生在，我想是在伦敦，莫特莱克，我想是这样。

sentences.en: He's sort of 16th century.
sentences.zh: 他算是16世纪的人。

sentences.en: But what's so interesting about him, you know, he's a fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 但他最有趣的地方在于，你知道，他是剑桥大学三一学院的院士。

sentences.en: He's the rector at Upton on Seven.
sentences.zh: 他是厄普顿塞文河畔的教区牧师。

sentences.en: He's got this fantastic library.
sentences.zh: 他拥有一个很棒的图书馆。

sentences.en: He's really interested in maths.
sentences.zh: 他对数学非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He tries to redesign the calendar.
sentences.zh: 他试图重新设计历法。

sentences.en: He coins the phrase British Empire.
sentences.zh: 他创造了“大英帝国”这个词。

sentences.en: Well, I was about to say, we should maybe come on back to the British Empire in just a second.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正想说，我们也许应该过一会儿再回到大英帝国的话题。

sentences.en: But just on all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但就这些东西而言，

sentences.en: So does that imply that the occult and astrology and all of the sort of stuff that seems to our sort of modern secular eyes more zany,
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着神秘学、占星术以及所有在我们现代世俗眼光看来更古怪的东西，

sentences.en: does that imply that that was part of a kind of continuum of learning and scholarship generally in the 16th century?
sentences.zh: 是否意味着那是16世纪普遍学习和学术连续体的一部分？

sentences.en: Or did people at the time, and I'm not asking this as a kind of rhetorical question, I genuinely don't know the answer.
sentences.zh: 还是当时的人们——我这不是在问反问句，我是真的不知道答案——

sentences.en: Did people at the time look at Dee and say, well, he knows a lot about maths, but that other stuff is completely bonkers.
sentences.zh: 当时的人们看迪伊时会说，嗯，他数学很好，但其他东西完全是疯话吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how did they, how was he perceived at the time?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他当时是如何被看待的？

sentences.en: Well, Dee is very much a Renaissance figure, perhaps in some ways, the most Renaissance figure that England ever produced,
sentences.zh: 嗯，迪伊在很多方面确实是一个文艺复兴时期的人物，也许是英国有史以来最典型的文艺复兴人物，

sentences.en: insofar as he is somebody proficient in sort of legitimate sciences that are regarded as lawful.
sentences.zh: 因为他精通被视为合法的科学。

sentences.en: So mathematics, for example, and he would have seen himself as being a learned astrologer, a learned mathematical astrologer.
sentences.zh: 比如数学，他会把自己看作是一位博学的占星家，一位博学的数学占星家。

sentences.en: And astrology in and of itself is not something that was regarded as a black art or an occult pursuit in a forbidden way.
sentences.zh: 占星术本身并不是一种被视为黑魔法或禁忌的神秘追求。

sentences.en: But yes, certainly when somebody gained that level of learning, then in the minds of others,
sentences.zh: 但确实，当一个人获得了那种程度的学识时，在他人眼中，

sentences.en: especially in the minds of the less learned and the unlearned, then that would blend into the idea that this person was a sorcerer, probably a sorcerer.
sentences.zh: 特别是在那些学识较少或无知的人眼中，那就会演变成这个人是个巫师的想法，很可能就是个巫师。

sentences.en: Because if you had access to that kind of secret knowledge, then you were probably going to be a sorcerer and you're going to use it to your own personal advantage.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你能接触到那种秘密知识，那么你很可能就是一个巫师，并且会利用它来谋取个人利益。

sentences.en: Now, Dee, ironically, spends his life defending himself against the charge that he is in any way a sorcerer and that he is not a conjurer.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，迪伊一生都在为自己辩护，反驳他是个巫师的指控，声称他不是个术士。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until years after his death that it emerges that he most definitely was a conjurer and was engaged in this practice of speaking to angels in a crystal through mediuMs.
sentences.zh: 直到他死后多年，人们才发现他绝对是个术士，并且从事着通过灵媒在水晶中与天使交谈的活动。

sentences.en: But Francis, so he doesn't think of himself as just, to use an anachronistic term, a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 但是弗朗西斯，他不认为自己只是——用一个时代错乱的词来说——一名科学家。

sentences.en: I mean, deep down, he knows he's a conjurer, does he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在内心深处，他知道自己是个术士，对吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he wouldn't have used the term scientist to describe himself,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不会用“科学家”这个词来描述自己，

sentences.en: but he might well have used the term science to describe what he was gaining from these angels through mediums,
sentences.zh: 但他很可能会用“科学”这个词来描述他通过灵媒从这些天使那里获得的东西，

sentences.en: the science of necromancy, as it's often described in medieval and early modern sources.
sentences.zh: 即招魂术的科学，正如在中世纪和近代早期文献中经常描述的那样。

sentences.en: The word science then, of course, having a much broader meaning than it does now.
sentences.zh: 当然，“科学”这个词在当时有着比现在宽泛得多的含义。

sentences.en: But yes, he saw himself as an adventurer in knowledge, I think it's fair to say,
sentences.zh: 但确实，我认为可以公平地说，他把自己看作是一个知识的冒险家，

sentences.en: and someone who was open to the possibility that knowledge might come through any avenue or almost any avenue.
sentences.zh: 一个对知识可能通过任何途径——或者几乎任何途径——获得持开放态度的人。

sentences.en: And I think that's what sets him apart as this Renaissance figure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是他作为文艺复兴人物的独特之处。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, early, you mentioned Rudolf II, the emperor in Prague at the end of the 16th century,
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，早些时候你提到了16世纪末布拉格的皇帝鲁道夫二世，

sentences.en: and John Dee goes to Prague and kind of mixes in that very, very kind of rich brew, the kind of Jewish traditions as well as Christian traditions and hermetic traditions.
sentences.zh: 约翰·迪伊去了布拉格，并融入了那种非常、非常丰富的氛围，包括犹太传统、基督教传统以及赫尔墨斯传统。

sentences.en: But Francis, am I right that, I mean, John Dee is also,
sentences.zh: 但是弗朗西斯，我说的对吗？我的意思是，约翰·迪伊也是，

sentences.en: obviously, he persuades people that he has these incredible powers, but he himself is convinced that he goes with a partner, doesn't he,
sentences.zh: 显然，他让人们相信他拥有这些不可思议的力量，但他自己也确信他和一个伙伴同行，不是吗？

sentences.en: who may have slightly been stringing Dee along.
sentences.zh: 那个伙伴可能稍微有点在利用迪伊。

sentences.en: Yes, this is Edward Kelly, who's just as fascinating a figure as Dee, if a slightly darker figure.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是爱德华·凯利，他是一个和迪伊一样迷人的人物，尽管是一个稍微阴暗一点的人物。

sentences.en: And yeah, Kelly is the long-term medium of Dee.
sentences.zh: 是的，凯利是迪伊长期的灵媒。

sentences.en: So he's the one who actually sees the angels in the crystal and reports to Dee what's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以他才是那个真正能在水晶中看到天使并向迪伊报告发生了什么的人。

sentences.en: And the most notorious incident that takes place is when Kelly basically says, the angels have commanded us that we should swap wives.
sentences.zh: 最臭名昭著的事件是凯利基本上说，天使命令我们应该交换妻子。

sentences.en: So I should sleep with your wife, you should sleep with mine.
sentences.zh: 所以我应该和你妻子睡觉，你应该和我妻子睡觉。

sentences.en: And Dee really struggles with this and thinks, well, you know, I know these angels, you know, they must be right because they've been right before.
sentences.zh: 迪伊对此非常挣扎，心想，嗯，你知道，我了解这些天使，它们一定是正确的，因为它们以前是对的。

sentences.en: And, you know, they must be sent by God because they've convinced me of that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它们一定是上帝派来的，因为它们让我相信了这一点。

sentences.en: But could this be that, you know, Kelly's actually just trying to sleep with my wife?
sentences.zh: 但这会不会是，你知道，凯利实际上只是想和我妻子睡觉？

sentences.en: And he agonizes and agonizes over it.
sentences.zh: 他为此痛苦万分。

sentences.en: And in the end, he convinces himself that, yes, this is a new kind of commandment from God, that God is abrogating the commandment against adultery, especially for him,
sentences.zh: 最后，他让自己相信，是的，这是上帝的一种新诫命，上帝正在废除反对通奸的诫命，特别是针对他，

sentences.en: and kind of convinces himself of this.
sentences.zh: 并且让自己相信了这一点。

sentences.en: But in a way, it kind of breaks him because he's almost tortured his conscience so much that he can no longer believe in himself.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这摧毁了他，因为他几乎折磨了自己的良心，以至于他再也无法相信自己了。

sentences.en: And he's a sort of a shell of a man after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他成了一个空壳般的人。

sentences.en: What's about the thing that Tom raised, I think, which is fascinating, about the British Empire, because he is the first person to use the phrase, the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 汤姆提到的关于大英帝国的事情怎么样？我认为这很迷人，因为他是第一个使用“大英帝国”这个词的人。

sentences.en: And as you said in the first half, there's always been this sense of Britain as exceptional because it's exceptionally magical and a place of wreathed in mystery
sentences.zh: 正如你在上半部分所说，人们一直有一种感觉，认为不列颠是独特的，因为它极其神奇，是一个笼罩在神秘之中的地方，

sentences.en: and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: So that phrase, the British Empire, does it, I mean, maybe this is stretching it too far, but does it have a kind of occult meaning?
sentences.zh: 所以“大英帝国”这个词，它——我的意思是，也许这有点牵强——它有一种神秘的含义吗？

sentences.en: It does for Dee, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对迪伊来说，绝对有。

sentences.en: When he talks about the British Empire, he's looking back rather than forward.
sentences.zh: 当他谈论大英帝国时，他是在回顾过去，而不是展望未来。

sentences.en: So he's looking back to an imagined empire that King Arthur and other British princes established in the New World.
sentences.zh: 所以他回顾的是亚瑟王和其他不列颠亲王在“新世界”建立的想象中的帝国。

sentences.en: So he becomes convinced, partly as a result of tales that are coming back from Spanish explorers, that they've met, you know, fair-skinned, fair-haired Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 因此，部分由于从西班牙探险家那里传回的故事，他确信他们遇到了，你知道，皮肤白皙、头发金黄的美洲原住民。

sentences.en: Speaking Welsh.
sentences.zh: 说着威尔士语。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: And so these kind of things, these traveller's tales, if you like, inspire Dee to suggest, well, maybe there was this empire that King Arthur extended into the New World.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西，这些旅行者的故事，如果你愿意的话，启发了迪伊去暗示，嗯，也许亚瑟王确实将帝国扩展到了新世界。

sentences.en: And of course, you've got the voyage of St. Brendan, which makes this plausible.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有圣布伦丹的航行，这使得这种说法变得可信。

sentences.en: So the voyage of St. Brendan, this legend that there's an Irish saint who gets in a coracle
sentences.zh: 所以圣布伦丹的航行，这个传说中有一位爱尔兰圣徒坐着皮划艇，

sentences.en: with his disciples and heads over to what appears to be the New World, these mysterious Western lands.
sentences.zh: 带着他的门徒前往看起来是新世界的地方，这些神秘的西方土地。

sentences.en: And so it's not for a 16th century observer, the idea that people might in the distant past have gone to the New World is by no means implausible.
sentences.zh: 所以对于16世纪的观察者来说，人们在遥远的过去可能去过新世界的想法绝非不可信。

sentences.en: And so, yeah,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，

sentences.en: the British Empire has this occult significance because it is through Merlin's extraordinary genius that Arthur is able to do things like design ships that are able to reach the New World or exploit the mineral resources that he finds there.
sentences.zh: 大英帝国具有这种神秘的意义，因为正是通过梅林非凡的天才，亚瑟王才能够做一些事情，比如设计能够到达新世界的船只，或者开发他在那里发现的矿产资源。

sentences.en: And Francis, presumably, this is part of the kind of the swirl of influences that impacts on Shakespeare's play, The Tempest, where you have Prospero, who is a magician,
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，据推测，这是影响莎士比亚戏剧《暴风雨》的各种影响因素的一部分，剧中有一个普洛斯彼罗，他是一位魔术师，

sentences.en: a conjurer on an island.
sentences.zh: 一个岛上的术士。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of echoes of English imperial projects in the Atlantic going on.
sentences.zh: 其中有各种各样关于大西洋英国帝国项目的回响。

sentences.en: Would that be a reasonable conclusion?
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的结论吗？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 噢，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think that in Prospero, we can see Merlin, we can see John Dee, we can see James I, you know, who fancies himself as this kind of magus-like figure.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在《暴风雨》中，我们可以看到梅林，可以看到约翰·迪伊，可以看到詹姆斯一世，你知道，他自诩为这种类似法师的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's all there.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这一切都在里面了。

sentences.en: And those sort of, you know, some of those abortive missions in the New World,
sentences.zh: 还有那些，你知道，在新大陆的一些失败的使命，

sentences.en: many of which didn't work and left these stranded communities and stranded people in the same way that Prospero finds himself stranded on an island.
sentences.zh: 其中许多都没有成功，留下了这些被困的社区和被困的人，就像普洛斯彼罗发现自己被困在岛上一样。

sentences.en: But also the contrast between Prospero's magic and the darker magic that Caliban represents, because he's the son of a witch, and she, you know,
sentences.zh: 但还有普洛斯彼罗的魔法与卡利班所代表的更黑暗的魔法之间的对比，因为他是女巫的儿子，而她，你知道，

sentences.en: has ruled the island with her dark magic.
sentences.zh: 用她的黑魔法统治着这个岛屿。

sentences.en: And now Prospero has come in with his good magic, which is very much the way that Dee would have thought of himself.
sentences.zh: 现在普洛斯彼罗带着他的善意魔法进来了，这非常像迪伊看待自己的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And I guess that, I mean, if you look at now in the war in Ukraine, the sense that people want to know what is happening,
sentences.zh: 我想，我的意思是，如果你看看现在的乌克兰战争，人们想要知道发生了什么的感觉，

sentences.en: that the sense that people want to know what will happen is kind of almost overpowering, really, really kind of urgent sense on both sides.
sentences.zh: 那种人们想要知道将会发生什么的感觉，几乎是压倒性的，在双方都有一种非常、非常迫切的感觉。

sentences.en: And so I guess that that would be a reason why, during the course of the civil wars in the 1640s, into Cromwell's protectorate.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这就是为什么在1640年代内战期间，一直到克伦威尔的护国公时期，

sentences.en: That really seems to amplify the role that particularly kind of prophets are playing, fortune tellers, people looking into the future.
sentences.zh: 这似乎真的放大了先知、算命师、预言未来的人所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: And actually, friend of the show, we're very keen on our dogs on this show.
sentences.zh: 事实上，作为节目的朋友，我们在这个节目里非常喜欢狗。

sentences.en: And of course, one of the most famous dogs in English history is Boy, the poodle owned by Prince Rupert of the Rhine, Cromwell's adversary at Marston Moor.
sentences.zh: 当然，英国历史上最著名的狗之一是“男孩”（Boy），那是莱茵的鲁珀特亲王的贵宾犬，他是克伦威尔在马斯顿荒原战役中的对手。

sentences.en: And Boy is supposed to be a medium.
sentences.zh: 而且“男孩”被认为是一个灵媒。

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Kind of letting Prince Rupert know all kinds of evil, dark things.
sentences.zh: 它似乎让鲁珀特亲王知道了各种邪恶、黑暗的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So Boy is, according to Puritan pamphleteers, Prince Rupert's witch is familiar.
sentences.zh: 所以根据清教徒小册子作者的说法，“男孩”是鲁珀特亲王的女巫使魔。

sentences.en: And in fact, according to one pamphlet, Boy was in fact a witch from Lapland who had transformed herself into canine shape and would run along at Prince Rupert's side,
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据一本小册子，“男孩”其实是一个来自拉普兰的女巫，她把自己变成了狗的形状，会在鲁珀特亲王身边跑来跑去，

sentences.en: giving him advanced intelligence to the movements of parliamentarian troops and so forth.
sentences.zh: 为他提供议会军动向的预警情报等等。

sentences.en: But, you know, this seems ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这看起来很荒谬。

sentences.en: And yet this had deadly consequences.
sentences.zh: 然而这却产生了致命的后果。

sentences.en: Could Prince Rupert interpret...
sentences.zh: 鲁珀特亲王能解读……

sentences.en: Did he really do it?
sentences.zh: 他真的这么做了吗？

sentences.en: Could Prince Rupert interpret Marx or did Boy speak real, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 鲁珀特亲王能解读马克思（Marx）吗？还是“男孩”真的会说话，多米尼克？

sentences.en: I don't think...
sentences.zh: 我不认为……

sentences.en: Yeah, but they must have thought about it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但他们肯定考虑过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, could Prince Rupert understand dog or did Boy speak English?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，鲁珀特亲王能听懂狗语，还是“男孩”会说英语？

sentences.en: I think some of the pamphlets claim that, yeah, that the dog would speak in a man's voice or a woman's voice to Rupert.
sentences.zh: 我想有些小册子声称，是的，那条狗会用男人的声音或女人的声音对鲁珀特说话。

sentences.en: But I mean, if it's a witch from Lapland, they don't speak English there.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，如果它是个来自拉普兰的女巫，那里的人不说英语。

sentences.en: Is Prince Rupert, is he well-traveled in Finland?
sentences.zh: 鲁珀特亲王去过芬兰吗？

sentences.en: I mean, come on.
sentences.zh: 拜托，别闹了。

sentences.en: The whole idea is laughable.
sentences.zh: 整个想法都很可笑。

sentences.en: Is it laughable?
sentences.zh: 很可笑吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Is it really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You really should be writing books on...
sentences.zh: 你真的应该写书关于……

sentences.en: A top historian.
sentences.zh: 一位顶级历史学家。

sentences.zh: 我以前没意识到那是那么晚的传统。

sentences.zh: 但有一个关于灵媒的迷人故事，她确实被正式指控了，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 所以你能最后给我们讲讲关于她的事吗？

sentences.en: Yes, this is the extraordinary case of Helen Duncan, who was an established medium in Portsmouth.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是海伦·邓肯的非凡案例，她是朴茨茅斯的一位知名灵媒。

sentences.en: And she, in 1943, claims during a seance to materialise the shape of a sailor who has just drowned in a ship that sunk.
sentences.zh: 1943年，她在降神会期间声称让一名刚在沉没船只中溺水的海员的形象显现出来。

sentences.zh: 而在这次显现中，因为她，无论她用什么手段，她制造了这些看似是人的幽灵。

sentences.zh: 这很不寻常，因为通常在这个时候，如果你想阻止某人算命或举行降神会，你会使用1824年的《流浪者法案》，

sentences.zh: 该法案在很大程度上已经取代了旧的《巫术法案》。

sentences.en: But the old Witchcraft Act made it a criminal offence to pretend to powers of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但旧的《巫术法案》规定，假装拥有巫术能力是一种刑事犯罪。
